sections.title: Identification and form
sections.text: This entry represents Solanum lycopersicum, the tomato; Lycopersicon esculentum is an older synonym. Native to the Andes, it is now cultivated worldwide. In cultivation it is an annual herb; in tropical climates it can become perennial and reach about 2 m.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The leaves are compound and the flowers are yellow. The fruit is a berry whose size, shape and colour vary widely among cultivars.

sections.title: Edibility and toxicity
sections.text: Ripe fruits are eaten raw or cooked. Green parts of the plant and unripe fruits contain glycoalkaloids, including α-tomatine; they should not be treated as equivalent to ripe fruit.
